Towers with podiums or spires come out far too big. In existing-building mode the 'servers fit' MW range then runs from an inflated hall area. At 555 W Hastings it hits the 40 MW cap.

suggested_fix: unverified — needs J.B. (e.g. footprint × own height per building, and check against the vanEnergyReport GFAs)

tool_says: register: "nameplate claim × utilisation 0.20–0.60 ... the low end of the band should be 0.20, not 0.35"; engine.js: lf:0.6 and "${mw} MW × 8,760 h × ${R.lf} average load"
problem: The register's range 0.20–0.60 for actual IT load against nameplate is not implemented. Every annual MWh figure in the tool (server electricity, heat, solar share, water, grid CO2) uses the single point 0.6, which is the top of the register's own band. The engine header promises 'ranges, never points'. If the low end (0.20) is right, these figures could be up to 3× too high.

tool_says: "nameplate claim × utilisation 0.20–0.60"; "colocation server utilisation 0.21→0.35 (LBNL 2024)"
problem: LBNL's 21%→35% is server utilisation (a share of operating time, i.e. processor activity), not power drawn as a share of nameplate. Servers draw a large share of peak power when idle. Multiplying nameplate MW by server utilisation mixes two different metrics. LBNL's 50% 'capacity utilization' is an assumption it uses to turn energy into power, not a measurement.
evidence: LBNL-2001637 (Dec 2024) p.28: "Colocation data centers average 21% utilization in 2014, rising to 35% in 2027." Exec. summary p.7: "Assuming an average capacity utilization rate of 50%".
suggested_fix: Label 0.21→0.35 as server utilisation (not a power factor), and the 0.5 as LBNL's assumption; whether either belongs in the MW band is unverified — needs J.B.

tool_says: "average ÷ peak ≈ 0.6 (Fan et al. 2007)"; load_factor: "≈ 0.6 facility level"
problem: In Fan et al., 0.595 is the real datacenter's average power as a share of its 'actual peak' (the summed achievable peak of the machines), measured at cluster level. Average ÷ observed peak is 0.83. 'Facility level' and plain 'peak' overstate what the paper shows.
evidence: Fan, Weber, Barroso 2007, Table 3 'Real DC': Average Power 59.5%, Observed Peak 71.9%, Average/Observed 82.8%; caption: normalized to actual peak, cluster level.
suggested_fix: "average ≈ 0.6 of actual (summed machine) peak, cluster-level measurement (Fan et al. 2007, Table 3); average ÷ observed peak 0.83"

tool_says: "Telia Helsinki snapshot ERF 0.75 and PUE 1.152 with 4.11 MW waste heat imply 4.8 MW actual against 24 MW IT nameplate = 0.20"
problem: The arithmetic is right if ERF = 4.11 MW ÷ total facility power: 4.11/0.75/1.152 = 4.76 MW, and 4.76/24 = 0.198. But Telia never defines ERF. If the reused energy counted is the 5.65 MW delivered, the same steps give 6.54 MW and 0.27. So the 0.20 low end rests on an unstated definition, from a one-day operator claim.
evidence: Telia PDF p.05: "Waste heat: 4.11 MW", "Total capacity back to the district heating: 5.65 MW", "PUE: 1.152", "ERF: 0.75"; p.12 lists ERF only as an abbreviation. 5.65/0.75/1.152 = 6.54 MW.
suggested_fix: unverified — needs J.B. (state the ERF definition assumed, label as operator claim, show both readings 0.20–0.27)

evidence: Telia PDF: "total power capacity of 100 MW and an IT capacity of 24 MW" (printed p.03); "As of 29.5.2024" snapshot (printed p.05).
suggested_fix: unverified — needs J.B. (confirm which page numbering is cited)

tool_says: "32.5 GWh non-heat ≈ 3.7 MW average for the whole 73,000 m² tower ... so the ≥3.7 MW of operator nameplate claims cannot all be running at once"
problem: The figure being compared is an annual average (3.71 MW) for the whole building, offices included. That rules out the claims (VAN5 1.6 + VAN-2 2.14 = 3.74 MW) running at full nameplate all year. It does not rule out them all running at once for a short time. Also, 'non-heat' is taken to be electricity, which is an assumption (the file's derivation note says 'assumed electricity'). The arithmetic is correct: 1.84 × 73,225 = 134,734 GJ = 37.4 GWh; 117,160 GJ = 32.5 GWh; ÷ 8,760 = 3.71 MW.
evidence: data/vancouver_energy_report.json derivation: "non-heat = total − heat (assumed electricity)"; sources/01 line 22: "Sum of claims ≥3.7 MW (VAN5 1.6 + VAN-2 2.14 + VAN1 unstated)".
suggested_fix: "... so the ≥3.7 MW of operator nameplate claims (claims) cannot all run at full load continuously"

tool_says: "111 E 5th 0.45 MW (no data centre yet)"

evidence: data/vancouver_energy_report.json 111 E 5th: heat_GJm2 0, ghg_kgm2 0, nonheat_GJ 14069 = total_GJ 14069.
suggested_fix: "111 E 5th 0.45 MW total (all-electric; heating included; no data centre yet)"

where: tool/engine.js:25 (R.cop), engine.js:289-290 calc(), cards.js:65-74, compare.js:17-18, extras.js:126,178 vs register quantities[cop].formula / inputs
tool_says: register: "COP = η × T_lm,sink ÷ (T_lm,sink − T_lm,source) ... inputs: heat_temp, receiver_temp"; code: "cop:[3.0,4.5]" used as fixed bounds everywhere
problem: The register's COP method (Lorenz, driven by heat temperature and receiver temperature) is not built. The code uses a fixed COP of 3.0–4.5 for every cooling type, receiver, network temperature and city. So heat_temp (air 25–35 / liquid 50–60) never enters any calculation. The register's 'two runs if unknown' for heat_temp is also not built. The register's coef only says 'tool range 3.0–4.5', and the quantity is still titled 'Heat-pump COP (Lorenz)'.
evidence: grep across the tool JS: no Lorenz, η or log-mean code. COP appears only as R.cop[0]/R.cop[1]. My recomputation of the register's own formula with η 0.45, source 55→45 °C, sink 70→40 °C (the register's liquid-cooled case) gives a COP far above 4.5. So the fixed range does not reflect the register's heat_temp.
suggested_fix: Either build the Lorenz formula with heat_temp and receiver_temp, or restate the register formula as 'fixed range 3.0–4.5 (DEA/Odense)' and drop heat_temp and receiver_temp as inputs. Needs J.B.

suggested_fix: Either label fac as 'power at full IT load (servers × PUE)' or show the average as mw × PUE × 0.6. Needs J.B. to choose.

problem: FEMP BMP #10 does not contain any of the three items attributed to it. The physics is sound: 3,600 kJ/kWh ÷ 2,400 kJ/kg = 1.5 kg/kWh, and B = E/(C−1) follows algebraically from the FEMP balance if drift is ignored. But the attribution is wrong. The register marks femp 'verified: true' with confidence 100/90/60 for these terms.
evidence: https://www.energy.gov/node/849241 (direct WebFetch was blocked by provenance, but the page was retrieved after a search hit). It gives no rate: 'Make-Up = Evaporation + Blowdown + Drift'; C 'approximately equal to the ratio of volume of make-up to blowdown'; 'Many systems operate at two to four cycles … six cycles or more may be possible'; no WUE/ISO. EPA WaterSense §6.3 Eq. 6-3–6-5, pp. 6-10–6-11, likewise no latent-heat value; rule of thumb p. 6-9: evaporation ≈1% of recirculating flow per 10 °F drop (≈2,330 kJ/kg effective, consistent with ~1.5 L/kWh).

tool_says: name "Generator NOx and PM", formula "AP-42 factor × rated hp × hours", coef "NOx 0.024 lb/hp·h uncontrolled"
problem: The quantity is named NOx and PM, but the register gives no PM coefficient and the tool shows NOx only. The PM factor (0.0007 lb/hp-h, about 0.43 g/kWh) is held only in genset_test. The formula also says "rated hp", but the code uses facility load (MW × PUE) × 4 h in kWh × 14.6 g/kWh.
evidence: engine.js:487 "${rng(gen[0]*14.6/1000,...,'kg NOₓ')}". No PM term in engine.js or addons.js. 15d:79: "≈0.43 g PM/kWh_e". Check: 0.024 × 453.6 ÷ 0.7457 = 14.60 g/kWh, correct. 0.0007 × 453.6 ÷ 0.7457 = 0.426 g/kWh.
suggested_fix: Add PM 0.0007 lb/hp-h (≈0.43 g/kWh, AP-42 Table 3.4-1, as in 15d) to the coef and either show PM in the tool or rename the quantity to NOx only. State the kWh basis (facility MW × PUE × 4 h).

tool_says: formula "charge × 3%/yr × GWP"; coef "IPCC GWPs; chillers 50–600 kg charge"; sources ["eccc"]; conf 90; status "in hand"
problem: No cited source supports any coefficient. 'eccc' is the Climate Normals CSV. The 3%/yr leak rate and the 50–600 kg charge range have no source in sources/*.md. The IPCC assessment report (AR4/AR5/AR6) and the refrigerant are not named. Conf 90 ("regulation, tariff or standard read directly") and "in hand" overstate it; on the scale this is 20 (judged) or 0 (gap). The quantity is not computed anywhere in the tool JS.

where: formula_register.json quantities[refuge_people].formula and tool/opps.json quantities[refuge_people]; source_roles ess
tool_says: usable area ÷ 3.5 m²; 2 m between beds
problem: The two coefficients don't fit together, and the register doesn't say which city each one applies to. JIBC's 3.5 m² is a 1.5 × 2.5 m sleeping space that already includes 0.75 m between beds. Edmonton's figure is 2 m between beds. At 2 m spacing a person needs more than 3.5 m², so dividing by 3.5 m² overstates Edmonton capacity. Example, assuming a 0.75 m cot (my assumption, not from a source): (0.75 + 2) × 2.5 ≈ 6.9 m² per person, about half the capacity. This also treats the two cities differently without saying so (parity).
evidence: JIBC Intro to Group Lodging, Sleeping Area Set Up (https://igl.jibc.ca/module-3-working-in-a-group-lodging-facility/group-lodging-set-up/sleeping-area-set-up/): "minimum sleeping area per person is 3.5 square metres (1.5 metres x 2.5 metres)"; "0.75 metres (2.5 feet) between beds". City of Edmonton Minimum Emergency Shelter Standards 2021 (https://www.gov.edmonton.ab.ca/sites/default/files/public-files/MinimumEmergencyShelterStandards.pdf): "2 meters between beds, if in a congregate setting".
suggested_fix: Write it per city: Vancouver (BC ESS/JIBC) area ÷ 3.5 m² with 0.75 m between beds; Edmonton 2 m between beds (no area per person given). The per-person area at 2 m depends on bed size: unverified — needs J.B.

tool_says: BC ESS / JIBC group lodging 3.5 m² per person; Edmonton shelter standard 2 m between beds; Health Canada cleaner-air spaces MERV 13+, 2–3 ACH (Formulas sheet)
problem: One source id holds three different documents, each cited only as 'Formulas sheet', with no URL, title or date. The register still marks it verified=true at conf 90 ('read directly'). The primary documents exist and say what is quoted, but some details differ. The Edmonton figure comes from a 2021 'Minimum Emergency Shelter Standards' PDF and applies only 'if in a congregate setting'. The 2024 Best Practices Guide calls 2 m 'optimal' and says the guide is 'aspirational'. 'ACH' is not the source's term (see the clean_air_volume finding).
evidence: JIBC page above (3.5 m², 0.75 m); Edmonton Minimum Emergency Shelter Standards 2021: "2 meters between beds, if in a congregate setting"; Edmonton Emergency Shelter Best Practices Guide 2024 p.20: "a minimum of two metres between beds is optimal"; p.5 "designed to be aspirational".
suggested_fix: Split ess into three source ids with their primary URLs: JIBC IGL Sleeping Area Set Up; City of Edmonton Minimum Emergency Shelter Standards (2021); Health Canada Guidance for Cleaner Air Spaces (Sept 2020). Add the 'congregate setting' qualifier.

tool_says: cleaned airflow ÷ (2–3 ACH); MERV 13+; < 26 °C
problem: Health Canada never uses 'ACH'. Its 2–3 figure is for portable air cleaners only: the clean air delivery rate for smoke should be 'at least' 2–3 times the room volume per hour. MERV 13 applies to central HVAC filters. The formula reads as a general ventilation rate for the room, which is broader than the source. The arithmetic itself (CADR ÷ 2–3 per hour = room volume) is right. Dates and the 26 °C match: published September 2020, 'Temperature should be kept below 26 °C'.
evidence: https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/publications/healthy-living/guidance-cleaner-air-spaces-during-wildfire-smoke-events.html (Sept 2020, modified 2020-11-13): "for smoke at least two to three times the room volume per hour" (portable air cleaner section); "A MERV value of 13 or more is recommended".
suggested_fix: portable-cleaner CADR (smoke) ÷ (at least 2–3 room volumes per hour); central HVAC filter MERV 13+; temperature below 26 °C (Health Canada 2020)

tool_says: spare cooling kW ÷ (0.108 kW per seated person + envelope gains); keep ≤ 26 °C
problem: The units don't work. Envelope gains are a total load in kW for the room, not a per-person figure, so they can't be added to 0.108 kW per person inside the divisor. As written, a large room's envelope load would be counted once per person. The load from outdoor ventilation air is also missing. Not yet computed in the tool code (no code found), so no displayed number is affected.
evidence: Recomputation of units: kW ÷ (kW/person + kW) is not in persons. Correct form: (spare kW − envelope kW − ventilation kW) ÷ 0.108 kW/person.
suggested_fix: (spare cooling kW − envelope and ventilation gains kW) ÷ 0.108 kW per seated person; keep ≤ 26 °C

tool_says: 26 °C Health Canada 2026
problem: The 2026 guidance sets 26 °C for older adults' homes. It says it was written for residential housing and that other settings need further research. Applying it to a public cooling room stretches its stated scope. The 2020 Health Canada cleaner-air-space guidance gives 'below 26 °C' for public rooms of this kind and fits better.
evidence: https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/publications/healthy-living/guidance-upper-indoor-temperature-limits-protecting-older-adults.html (June 22, 2026): "upper indoor temperature limit of 26°C to protect older adults"; "developed for residential housing units".
suggested_fix: Cite as 26 °C for older adults' homes (Health Canada 2026), and the 2020 cleaner-air-space guidance ('below 26 °C') for public rooms.

tool_says: Vancouver Solar Access Guidelines (2024, am. 2026): fall-equinox shadows 10:00–16:00 (Formulas sheet)
problem: Vancouver has two solar access guidelines. The dates cited match only 'Areas Outside of Downtown' (approved 10 Jul 2024, amended 4 Feb 2026). The Downtown Peninsula guidelines (approved 17 Sep 2025, amended 29 Jul 2026) are not cited, yet they apply to downtown parcels such as the test parcel 1169 Richards St. They also differ: Robson Village is 10 am–3 pm, and the metric is a percentage of shadow coverage over 25 fifteen-minute intervals. 'Opposite sidewalks' applies only to village high streets outside downtown. Inside downtown it is the north sidewalks of Davie and Robson.
evidence: https://guidelines.vancouver.ca/guidelines-solar-access-areas-outside-downtown.pdf: "Approved by Council July 10, 2024", "Last amended February 4, 2026", fall equinox 10 a.m.–4 p.m. PDT. https://guidelines.vancouver.ca/guidelines-solar-access-downtown.pdf: approved Sept 17, 2025, amended July 29, 2026; Robson Village 10 am–3 pm; shadow % over 25 intervals.
suggested_fix: Cite both guidelines with URLs. Pick the one that applies by Downtown Peninsula boundary (Map 1). Add the Downtown time windows and protected spaces.

tool_says: unit "m²·h"; status "in hand"; conf 90
problem: Neither Vancouver guideline uses m²·h. Outside downtown the test is 'no new shadow' within park and school property lines, shown visually. Downtown uses a percentage. No code in the tool computes a shadow quantity; scene3d only draws shadows. The status 'in hand' at conf 90 describes the rule, not a figure the tool produces. The coefficient was also read through the Formulas sheet, not the guideline itself.
evidence: Outside-downtown guideline: no m²-hour or percentage threshold; compliance shown by shadow studies. grep of tool/*.js: no equinox or shadow-area calculation (only three.js castShadow/receiveShadow).
suggested_fix: Unit 'new shadow yes/no (outside downtown); % coverage (downtown)'. Status: rule in hand, not built.

tool_says: fall-equinox shadows 10:00–16:00 on parks, schools, opposite sidewalks
problem: The formula is Vancouver-only. In Edmonton (s. 7.140(9)) the study is discretionary, applies only to Discretionary Developments, uses four dates every 3 hours from sunrise to sunset (MST), and is measured against the maximum massing the zone allows. edm7140sun is still 'pending build'. I checked edm7140sun against the local copy of Bylaw 20001, and it is accurate.
evidence: /mnt/user-data/uploads/Claude Link/Bylaw20001.pdf p.994, s. 7.140 9.1: "may require ... where the proposed development is a Discretionary Development"; 9.2.3: "every 3 hours between sunrise and sunset Mountain Standard Time on March 21, June 21, September 21 and December 21"; 9.3.1 max allowable massing vs proposed.
suggested_fix: Add an Edmonton branch to the formula from s. 7.140(9) as quoted. In IH zones there are no discretionary uses, so no study can be required.

tool_says: const lw=[91+10*Math.log10(n),101+10*Math.log10(n)] … 'Cooling units: power at the meter … about one unit per MW'
problem: Each unit is about 1 MW of heat. The low bound, 91 dBA, is the low-noise rating of the smallest Trane unit (333 kW). A unit near 1 MW is rated 98 (low-noise) to 101 (standard). So at one unit per MW the low bound is about 7 dB too quiet. The low-noise limit distance is also understated by about 2.2×. For example, at 1 MW in a quiet zone the tool gives 79 m where a ~1 MW low-noise unit gives about 177 m. If the 91 dBA units were kept, about 3 units per MW would be needed: 91 + 4.8 = 95.8 dBA.
evidence: Trane RTAF-SLB001-GB_0620 p.13 (HSE R134a table, via WebFetch): size 090, 333 kW: SN 94 / LN 91; size 280, 1010 kW: SN 101 / LN 98. Recomputed: n=2 at 1 MW gives 94.0–104.0 dBA; with a per-unit 98–101 it gives 101.0–104.0 dBA.
suggested_fix: unverified — needs J.B. (either use the per-unit level matched to ~1 MW units, 98–101 dBA, or size the unit count to 333 kW units)

where: formula_register.json quantities[ev_stalls].formula; tool/opps.js:53 (EV charging hub physics) and tool/engine.js:486 ('EV charging, if 1 MW were set aside')
tool_says: formula: "P_reserved × SF ÷ P_charger"; code: const st=[500/19.2,500/7.4] → "1 MW set aside serves about 26–68 Level 2 stalls (7.4–19.2 kW, 0.5 diversity)"
problem: The simultaneity factor is applied the wrong way round. Silber et al. define it as the share of installed charger power drawn at once. So a fixed reservation supports N = P ÷ (SF × P_charger), not P × SF ÷ P_charger. The tool's formula halves the 1 MW and then assumes every charger runs at full power, which is the same as SF = 1 on 500 kW. The result is 4× too low (1/SF²). If the SF 0.5 premise is kept: 1,000 ÷ (0.5 × 19.2) = 104 and 1,000 ÷ (0.5 × 7.4) = 270 stalls, against the 26–68 shown. The m² figures that follow (573–1,486 m²) and the opps.js:54 land check (need = st[1]×22) are scaled down by the same factor.
evidence: Silber et al. abstract (publikationen.bibliothek.kit.edu/1000163825): simultaneity factor is "the share of installed power related to the theoretical maximum power". Recomputed: 500/19.2=26.0, 500/7.4=67.6 vs 1000/(0.5×19.2)=104.2, 1000/(0.5×7.4)=270.3.
suggested_fix: Unverified, needs J.B.'s decision. With the definition as read, the formula would be P_reserved ÷ (SF × P_charger), giving about 104–270 Level 2 stalls per MW at SF 0.5. Whether SF 0.5 should apply to Level 2 at all is a separate question (see the next finding).

tool_says: "Level 2 stalls (7.4–19.2 kW, 0.5 diversity)"; register coef "SF 0.5" sourced to silber2024

That is a transfer to another charger class and use pattern, and the tool does not say so. Workplace and depot Level 2 sessions are long and overlap, so their simultaneity can be much higher. The register also lists silber2024 at confidence 70 ('peer-reviewed coefficient transferred') without saying it covers fast charging only.
evidence: Silber abstract: "in most cases, fast-charging sites can be designed with a simultaneity factor of 0.5". sources/06 also lists NREL "25–100% peak plug utilisation".
suggested_fix: Unverified, needs J.B. At least say that 0.5 comes from DC fast-charging sites, or find a Level 2 workplace simultaneity source.

The code takes $/MWh of gas energy (no ÷0.85) and nets it against heat-pump electricity per MWh of heat, then labels the result 'per MWh of heat'. Gas and heat units are mixed, and the heat's value is understated by 15%. The displayed Vancouver net value comes out about $6/MWh too low compared with the register's method.

suggested_fix: Either apply ÷0.85 in ECON.gas (Vancouver 39.41, Edmonton 10.60 $/MWh heat) to match the register, or state in the register and card that the value is per MWh of gas displaced and convert the heat-pump term to match. Which to choose needs J.B.

tool_says: With space heat 61% and DHW/losses flat (STRATEGO), peak month ÷ minimum month = 3.9 Vancouver, 3.3 Edmonton; ... provincial space-heat share from CEUD 2023: BC 0.46, AB 0.63 (replaces national 0.61 in the profile)

(b) 0.46 and 0.63 are space heating as a share of ALL residential energy, appliances and lighting included. In a heat-demand profile, the flat part should be DHW as a share of heat (space + water). Used that way, the shares change the ratios, and Edmonton moves from lower than Vancouver to higher.

suggested_fix: Recompute the peak/minimum ratios with whichever share is adopted, and update the status line. Using space ÷ (space + water) (BC 0.63, AB 0.73 from CEUD 2023) fits a heat profile better. The final choice is unverified and needs J.B.

suggested_fix: Q[kW] = flow[L/s] × 4.18 × ΔT[K] (÷1000 for MW). Call 11 °C a 'KWL model constraint' and add the 6 °C minimum.

It ranks them only ahead of large data centres that are not tethered (s. 6), not ahead of every load. Tethering can also use an existing generator declared underutilized (s. 5(4)(a)), so 'new' is not required. The alberta.ca/datacentres/grid page (fetched) gives the 'front of the connection line' sentence and states no MW threshold.
suggested_fix: Alberta: under Alta Reg 117/2026, data centres drawing ≥75 MW from transmission that tether to their own generation or storage (new, or existing and underutilized) are processed ahead of untethered large data centres (s. 2, 5, 6). Does not apply below 75 MW or on distribution service.

tool_says: gen=[fac[0]*1000*4,fac[1]*1000*4] ... 'about 4 full-load hours a year: … t CO₂ and … kg NOₓ a year (uncontrolled-engine upper bound)'; genCard: 'up to ${fmt(gen[0])} t CO₂'
problem: The register formula is energy = units × kW × test hours, meaning installed generator capacity. The code uses facility load (IT MW × PUE) in its place. plant.js:29 sizes gN = gNeed plus N+1 or N+2 spares, so installed capacity (gN × g.mw) is larger than facility load. Every unit is tested at 100 % load (AUC 27938), so the shown figure is not an 'upper bound' or an 'up to'. It understates by the spare fraction. Separately, energyView prints the generator-testing emissions unconditionally, even when the user chose no generators (A.gens==='none'). genCard checks this; energyView does not.
evidence: plant.js:29 'gNeed=…Math.ceil(Q/g.mw), gN=g?spare(gNeed,A.genSpares||'n1')'; AUC 27938-D01-2023 ¶8 (fetched): at 100 % load 'one generator is tested per day for up to two hours, twice a year' — each unit at its own rating. engine.js:487 has no gens check.
suggested_fix: Use installed capacity (s.gN × s.g.mw × 1000 kW) × 4 h, as the register says. Hide the energyView generator line when A.gens==='none'.

tool_says: q = 12 W/m ground-only to 19 W/m with a dry cooler (derived from Zurmuhl et al. 2018, a 14.5 kW data centre, Ithaca, k 3.27 W/m·K)

So 12 W/m (1,248 m base field) vs 19 W/m (760 m optimised field) is a base-vs-optimised difference, not ground-only vs hybrid. Also, 14.5 kW is the equipment cooling load, not the heat sent to the ground: the ground also takes the heat pump's compressor work, and in the hybrid case the dry cooler takes part of the heat. Yet the register formula divides 'heat to ground (W)' by a q that was derived from the cooling load.
evidence: Zurmuhl 2018, https://pangea.stanford.edu/ERE/pdf/IGAstandard/SGW/2018/Zurmuhl.pdf, p.7 s.4.2.1: 'The economically optimal value is approximately 760 m' (GHP, Fig. 4); p.8 s.4.2.2: hybrid run 'for the previously optimized BHE length of 760 m'; p.2: '14.5 kWth' equipment cooling load. Recomputed: 14,500/1,248 = 11.6 W/m; 14,500/760 = 19.1 W/m.
suggested_fix: Relabel as '12 W/m (base 1,248 m field) to 19 W/m (economically optimised 760 m field, ground-only GHP; the hybrid was also run at 760 m)', and say q is cooling load per metre, not ground heat rejection per metre. Correct q for ground rejection: unverified — needs J.B.

where: tool/engine.js:126 plantPerMW(); used at engine.js:161–165 (mathNeeds), 287 (calc r.plant), 346, 270, 471 (roof share for solar)

where: tool/cards.js:38 and :66-71 (heatEcon); tool/engine.js:265-266 (heat tab sentence); register price_ceiling / condition e_savings, e_window
tool_says: gas:{van:9.305*3.6,edm:(1.045+1.458)*3.6}, // $/MWh of gas energy displaced ... const net=[v-pe/cop[0],v-pe/cop[1]]
problem: The register defines the buyer ceiling (what the receiver saves) as 'fuel price ÷ boiler efficiency (0.85)'. The tool uses the raw gas price per MWh of gas and sets it against heat-pump electricity per MWh, with no 0.85. Demand comes from CEUD, which counts delivered fuel, not useful heat (the cards.js:107 comment says so). So each MWh of gas is treated as needing a full MWh of heat-pump heat. The receiver's saving per MWh of heat is understated by 15%, and the 'net' value, break-even distances and payback are skewed. Vancouver net: tool $10.9–18.4/MWh; with ÷0.85 it is $16.8–24.3/MWh (+35–55%). Edmonton: tool −$7.6 to −$2.0; with ÷0.85 it is −$6.0 to −$0.45.
evidence: formula_register.json quantities.price_ceiling.formula: 'fuel price ÷ boiler efficiency (0.85)'. Recomputed: Van v=9.305×3.6=33.50, pe=67.9, so 33.50−67.9/3=10.87 and 33.50−67.9/4.5=18.41. With 33.50/0.85=39.41 these become 16.78 and 24.32. Edm pe=43.68+2.53+0.0809×43.68=49.74, v=9.01, so −7.57 and −2.04. With 9.01/0.85=10.60 they become −5.98 and −0.45.
suggested_fix: Apply the register's ÷0.85 (gas-heated receivers), or convert CEUD delivered energy to useful heat (×0.85) before costing heat-pump electricity. The formula change is confirmed from the register; J.B. to choose how.

where: tool/cards.js:38 (ECON.gas.edm); feeds the engine.js:266 statement 'no route pays back at any distance' for Edmonton
tool_says: ATCO Mid Use delivery 1.045 + Alberta regulated rate Oct 2026 1.458 $/GJ (riders excluded)
problem: An annual heating saving is valued at one shoulder month's regulated gas rate (October 2026, $1.458/GJ). Heating demand peaks in winter, when the ATCO-area rate ran $2.4–3.4/GJ. The 12-month average (Nov 2025–Oct 2026) is $2.025/GJ, 39% above October. Vancouver uses FortisBC's quarterly cost of gas, so the two cities are treated unequally. Combined with the missing ÷0.85, the Edmonton best case turns positive: (1.045+2.025)×3.6/0.85 = $13.00/MWh against $11.05 of heat-pump electricity at COP 4.5, or +$1.95/MWh. That contradicts the verdict-like sentence 'the heat pump's electricity costs more than the gas the heat would replace ... so no route pays back at any distance'.
evidence: ucahelps.alberta.ca/regulated-rates.aspx (fetched 17 Oct 2026), ATCO Gas Default Rate Tariff $/GJ. 2026: Jan 3.331, Feb 2.422, Mar 1.784, Apr 1.874, May 0.936, Jun 2.076, Jul 1.595, Aug 1.729, Sep 1.124, Oct 1.458. 2025: Nov 2.579, Dec 3.390. 12-month mean = 24.298/12 = 2.025. tool_says: Alberta: micro-generation ≤ 5 MW and ≤ the site's annual use, retail credit under 150 kW, pool price above.
problem: The regulation caps nameplate capacity at the lesser of 5 MW or the customer's service rating. Annual consumption is an intent test ('all or a portion of'), not the stated cap.
evidence: AUC Micro-generation Notice Submission Guideline 2026 (media.auc.ab.ca/.../MicrogenerationNoticeSubmissionGuideline2026.pdf), quoting Reg. s. 1(1)(h): "does not exceed the lesser of five megawatts or the rating of the customer's service"; "intended to meet all or a portion of the customer's total energy consumption".
suggested_fix: '≤ the lesser of 5 MW or the customer's service rating, sized to meet all or part of the site's own consumption; small <150 kW retail credit, large 150 kW–5 MW hourly pool price.'

tool_says: register: "Vancouver I-3 to 30.5 m ... I-3 caps building width and depth at 61 m" | tool: "Height 18.3 m (City may allow 30.5 m). ... Buildings at most 61 m wide and deep."
problem: The I-3 sub-area A schedule allows a further discretionary increase to 45.7 m (s. 3.1.2.11). The Director of Planning may also increase the 61 m depth and width where there is a functional need (s. 3.1.2.19). Both texts present lower or harder limits than the schedule.
evidence: data/raw/van/i3.txt (I-3 schedule, June 2026): 3.1.2.10 "height not exceeding 30.5 m"; 3.1.2.11 "Despite section 3.1.2.10 ... a height not exceeding 45.7 m"; 3.1.2.19 "may increase the maximum building depth or building width where a functional need is demonstrated".
suggested_fix: 'Height 18.3 m (City may allow 30.5 m, or 45.7 m under s. 3.1.2.11). Buildings 61 m wide and deep unless the Director of Planning increases it for functional need (s. 3.1.2.19).'

tool_says: FC-2 to 51.8 m | "Height 10.7–22.9 m (City may allow up to 51.8 m)"
problem: The 51.8 m relaxation applies only in sub-areas A/B (s. 3.1.2.7) and C2/D (s. 3.3.2.7). C1 can go to 18.3 m and E to 42.7 m. 'Up to 51.8 m' is correct as a ceiling but is not true for every FC-2 parcel.
evidence: data/raw/van/fc2.txt: 3.2.2.7 "height not exceeding 18.3 m" (C1); 3.4.2.7 "height not exceeding 42.7 m" (E); 3.1.2.7 and 3.3.2.7 "not exceeding 51.8 m".
suggested_fix: Add 'depending on sub-area (C1 18.3 m, E 42.7 m)'.

tool_says: I-2 s. 2.2.7, I-3 s. 2.2.11, FC-2 s. 2.2.4: bulk data storage not permitted at the ground floor except entrances.

tool_says: ≈2 ha per MW rejected to ground alone
problem: Zurmuhl 2018 does not state 2 ha per MW. It is derived (12 W/m, 150 m holes, 36 m² each) from a 14.5 kW Ithaca field at k 3.27, and should be labelled derived. The register's own borefield coef gives Edmonton 7–11 W/m. That works out to about 2.2–3.4 ha per MW, so one figure for both cities understates Edmonton.
evidence: Recomputed: 1,000,000 W ÷ 12 W/m = 83,333 m ÷ 150 = 556 holes × 36 m² = 2.0 ha. At 7 W/m: 952 × 36 = 3.4 ha; at 11 W/m: 2.2 ha. sources/15c line 194 labels it "Worked example (derived)". AB setbacks (1 m building, 3 m property line, 15 m water well) confirmed in data/AB_Directive_Water_Wells_GSHE_2018.pdf Table 4.
suggested_fix: '≈2 ha per MW (derived, Ithaca ground); ≈2.2–3.4 ha in Edmonton ground (scaling assumed)'.

where: formula_register.json quantities.ambient_cover (coef, status, source_roles bylaw14600); source string bylaw14600
tool_says: "Edmonton Bylaw 14600 limits pending (J.B. retrieval D1)"; status "Vancouver in hand; Edmonton to recheck"; bylaw14600: "ss.19–22: 65 dBA day / 50 night at the residential property line"
problem: The consolidated Bylaw 14600 (22 Oct 2024) is already in data/, and the tool already uses its limits ('50 dBA next to homes, 60 dBA next to other uses'). The register still calls Edmonton 'pending'. The source string cites ss.19–22 but gives only the residential limits (ss.19–20). The 60 dBA night non-residential limit the tool uses (s.22), and 75 dBA day (s.21), are not in the register text.
evidence: data/Edmonton_Bylaw_14600_Community_Standards_2024-10-22.pdf s.20(1): "any sound exceeding 50 dB(A), as measured at the property line of a property zoned for use as residential, before 7 a.m. or after 10 p.m."; s.22(1): "exceeding 60 dB(A) … zoned for use other than residential"; s.21(1): 75 dB(A) daytime non-residential.
suggested_fix: bylaw14600: 'ss.19–22 (consol. 22 Oct 2024): residential property line 65 dBA day / 50 night; other property 75 day / 60 night; short-duration day allowances s.19(3), 21(3); s.14 disturbance offence applies whether or not a limit is exceeded'; drop 'pending'.

tool_says: "the zone pair sets what is allowed; a louder zone is the cover — Vancouver credits no ambient noise for equipment"
problem: The 'zone pair' logic is how Vancouver's By-law 6555 works (source zone × receiving zone). Edmonton's Bylaw 14600 sets limits by the receiving property's zoning only (residential or other), whatever zone the source is in. Edmonton also has a general disturbance offence (s.14) that applies whatever the dBA reading. The condition's formula describes one city's rule as if it covered both. The tool code itself handles Edmonton correctly (engine.js:565: residential 50, other 60).
evidence: Bylaw 14600 ss.19–22 (limits keyed only to 'property zoned for residential use' / 'other than residential'); s.14(3): guilty "whether or not the decibel level … exceeds any limit"; By-law 6555 ss.2.1–2.3 keyed to source zone and point-of-reception zone.
suggested_fix: Formula: 'Vancouver: source-zone × receiving-zone pair (By-law 6555 ss.2.1–2.3); Edmonton: receiving property's zoning only (Bylaw 14600 ss.19–22), plus the s.14 disturbance offence'.

where: source van6555zones (formula_register.json and opps.json); ambient_cover coef
tool_says: "'background noise' credited only for commercial premises (s.3.1(b)); no ambient credit for equipment"
problem: s.3.1(b) is not a credit. It is an extra prohibition: amplified music or voice in commercial premises must not exceed background + 3 dBA. Calling it 'credited' reverses the meaning. The zone-pair values quoted are correct, but they leave out quiet→other (60/55) and intermediate→quiet (60/50), which the tool does use (limQ intermediate = 50).
evidence: data/raw/van/6555.txt s.3.1(b)(i): sound "in commercial premises the level of which … exceeds 3 dBA above the background noise"; s.2.1(b)(ii) 55 dBA night quiet→other; s.2.2(b)(i) 50 dBA night intermediate→quiet.
suggested_fix: 'background noise appears only as a stricter test for amplified sound from commercial premises (s.3.1(b)); no ambient allowance for equipment'; list all six zone-pair values.

tool_says: register: "AUC Rule 012 road categories credit ambient but apply only to power plants and substations"; tool (both cities): "a tonal low-frequency sound adds 5 dBA in Alberta's rule — the kind neighbours describe most"
problem: Rule 012 applies to a wider set of facilities than power plants and substations: it also covers gas utility pipelines, hydro developments, energy storage facilities and transmission lines. That matters when a data centre has its own battery storage or generation. The tool's 'Low hum' row is shown in Vancouver as well, without saying that Rule 012 does not govern a data centre's cooling plant. It also omits that both criteria (dBC − dBA ≥ 20 AND a clear tone at 20–250 Hz) must be met. 'the kind neighbours describe most' has no cited source.
evidence: data/AUC_Rule_012_2024-09-30.pdf s.1.1(2): "'facility' means a gas utility pipeline, hydro development, power plant, substation, energy storage facility or transmission line"; s.4.5(2): "both criteria be fulfilled"; s.4.5(3): "five dBA must be added".
suggested_fix: Register: 'apply only to AUC facilities (power plants, substations, storage, lines, pipelines)'. Tool: 'Alberta's rule for energy facilities (not data centres) adds 5 dBA when a clear low tone and a dBC–dBA gap of 20 dB are both measured'; source or drop 'the kind neighbours describe most' (unverified — needs J.B.).

where: tool/opps.js:53 (EV charging hub, G.physics and G.land); tool/engine.js:486 (Electricity card); formula_register.md:129 (ev_stalls)
tool_says: 1 MW set aside serves about ${fmt(500/19.2)}–${fmt(500/7.4)} Level 2 stalls (7.4–19.2 kW, 0.5 diversity)  [displays 26–68 stalls]; register: "P_reserved × SF ÷ P_charger"
problem: The simultaneity factor is applied the wrong way round. Silber et al. define it as installed power as a share of the theoretical maximum, so a site of N chargers needs SF × N × P_charger of supply. The stalls a reserve can serve are therefore P ÷ (SF × P_charger), not P × SF ÷ P_charger. That gives 1000 ÷ (0.5 × 19.2) to 1000 ÷ (0.5 × 7.4) = 104–270 stalls, not 26–68. The displayed count is 4× too low. Every figure built on it is also wrong: the land gate threshold need = st[1]×22 = 1,487 m² should be about 5,946 m², and the engine.js parking area of about 573–1,486 m² should be about 2,292–5,946 m². Separately, the 0.5 comes from DC fast-charging sites in Germany and is being applied to Level 2. That transfer is not flagged.
evidence: Silber, Scheubner, Märtz 2024 abstract (https://publikationen.bibliothek.kit.edu/1000163825, fetched 17 Oct 2026): simultaneity factor is "the share of installed power related to the theoretical maximum power"; "fast-charging sites can be designed with a simultaneity factor of 0.5". Recomputed: 1000/(0.5×19.2)=104.2; 1000/(0.5×7.4)=270.3; 270.3×22=5,946 m².
suggested_fix: Formula should be stalls = P_reserved ÷ (SF × P_charger), giving about 104–270 Level 2 stalls per MW at SF 0.5. Land need is about 2,290–5,950 m² at 22 m² each. Label SF 0.5 as transferred from DC fast-charging sites (unverified for Level 2). Confirm with J.B.

suggested_fix: Show the result in kWh (8–42 kWh at 1 MW), or use more decimals for small values. The formula itself matches the register.

tool_says: About ${fmt(south)} m² of south-facing wall in total (the whole wall, as an upper bound)

A 45°-rotated footprint has 2,000 m² of SE+SW wall but the card reports 1,414 m². The figure is reasonable as a south-equivalent area, but 'the whole wall' and 'upper bound' don't describe it. The orientation handling itself is correct: local y is north (engine.js P(): y=(lat−lat0)·110540), and the sum gives the same result for CW and CCW rings.
evidence: Node test with the same loop: 60×40 m rectangle, H=20 → 1,200 m² for both windings. A 50 m square rotated 45°, H=20 → 1,414 m², against 2,000 m² of actual SE+SW wall.
suggested_fix: Change the wording to something like 'south-equivalent wall area (each wall weighted by how directly it faces south)'. Also fix the code comment '(y down)', because y is north-up.

where: tool/addons.js:160 genCard (Standby generators card, Testing row)
tool_says: gen=[fac*4*0.706/1000,fac*4*14.6/1000] → "about 4 full-load hours a year: up to ${fmt(gen[0])} t CO₂ and ${fmt(gen[1])} kg NOₓ (uncontrolled-engine upper bound, AP-42)"

The register formula is "units × kW × test hours at load", and each set, spares included, is load-tested at its own rating. The card's own unit count (s.gN × s.g.mw) is ignored. The 10.5 h a year of no-load running is also left out. So the card understates by the ratio of installed generator capacity to facility load.
evidence: Hand recompute, 1 MW IT: fac = 1×1.55×1000 = 1,550 kW; ×4 h = 6,200 kWh → 4.38 t CO₂, 90.5 kg NOx (what the card shows). plant.js:29: Q = 1.55 → gen1 (1.0 MW), gNeed = ceil(1.55/1.0) = 2, gN (n+1) = 3. Register formula: 3 × 1,000 kW × 4 h = 12,000 kWh → 8.47 t CO₂, 175 kg NOx, about 1.9× the card. formula_register genset_test: "energy = units × kW × test hours at load". AP-42 factors confirmed: NOx 0.024, PM 0.0007, CO₂ 1.16 lb/hp-hr → 14.6, 0.43, 706 g/kWh.
suggested_fix: Use s.gN × s.g.mw × 1000 × 4 h (matching the register), or drop "up to". The no-load fuel share is unverified — needs J.B.

tool_says: "L = heat to ground (W) ÷ q"; "q = 12 W/m ground-only to 19 W/m with a dry cooler (derived from Zurmuhl et al. 2018, a 14.5 kW data centre...)"

In the hybrid case the dry cooler takes part of the load, so 19 W/m is not a ground rejection rate. sources/15c line 188 applies (1 + 1/COP) to heat to ground and then divides by this load-based q, which counts the heat-pump input twice and oversizes by about 1.35×.
evidence: Zurmuhl 2018 (pangea.stanford.edu PDF, fetched): "approximate equipment cooling load of 14.5 kWth" (Sec. 3.1), Table 1 total borehole length 1248 m, optimal about 760 m. Recompute: 14,500/1,248 = 11.6 W/m; 14,500/760 = 19.1 W/m. Heat rejected to ground is not reported in the paper.
suggested_fix: Relabel the formula input as "cooling load sent to the borefield (W)" so it matches how q was derived.

tool_says: "land ≈2 ha per MW"

suggested_fix: "land ≈1.3–2 ha per MW at Ithaca ground; ≈2.2–3.4 ha in Edmonton (scaled, assumption); Vancouver not known"

The rule state 'na' means 'the rung does not bear on it', but BC has a rule: the Geothermal Resources Act covers water at 80 °C or above, and lower temperatures fall outside it. Edmonton gets its rule (AER D089) while Vancouver gets an opinion. The 'not plausible' judgement also rests on a gradient the project's own research marks as derived and UNVERIFIED. problem: Three slips against the project's own source notes. (1) Barth gives 'typical allowed' injection as 5–20 °C. 'Liquid-cooled only' implies liquid cooling is enough, but the register gives liquid-cooled heat at 50–60 °C, below both 65 °C and the 70–90 °C absorption minimum. suggested_fix: Align with the register: absorption needs ≥90 °C single-effect or 70–80 °C two-stage; liquid-cooled heat (50–60 °C) needs a heat-pump lift; adsorption ran at 45 °C (LRZ, operator claim) and ~65 °C (iDataCool). Final wording unverified — needs J.B.

where: tool/opps.js:53 (EV charging hub, physics gate); formula_register.json ev_stalls.formula; sources/06 §1
tool_says: const st=[500/19.2,500/7.4]; ... `1 MW set aside serves about ${fmt(st[0])}–${fmt(st[1])} Level 2 stalls (7.4–19.2 kW, 0.5 diversity)` | register: "P_reserved × SF ÷ P_charger"
problem: The simultaneity factor is applied in the wrong direction. Silber et al. define it as the site's installed (grid) power as a share of the chargers' theoretical maximum. So a 0.5 factor lets the same connection serve twice as many chargers: stalls = P ÷ (SF × P_charger). The tool and register multiply by 0.5 instead, so the tool shows 26–68 stalls per MW. The correct reading of the source gives about 104–270, a factor of 4 lower than it should be. The 22 m²/stall land check (opps.js:54) uses the same wrong stall count. Also, Silber's 0.5 is for DC fast-charging sites but is applied here to Level 2, and it is labelled 'diversity', which is a different term (a diversity factor is ≥ 1).
evidence: https://publikationen.bibliothek.kit.edu/1000163825 abstract: simultaneity factor is "the share of installed power related to the theoretical maximum power"; "fast-charging sites can be designed with a simultaneity factor of 0.5". Recompute: 1,000 kW ÷ (0.5 × 19.2) = 104; 1,000 ÷ (0.5 × 7.4) = 270. Tool: 1,000 × 0.5 ÷ 19.2 = 26; ÷ 7.4 = 68.
suggested_fix: stalls = P_reserved ÷ (SF × P_charger), i.e. 2000/19.2 – 2000/7.4 for 1 MW at SF 0.5. Whether a fast-charging factor fits Level 2 is unverified — needs J.B.

The ~1.5 L/kWh bound is sound physics (3,600 ÷ ~2,400 kJ/kg), but attributing it to FEMP at confidence 100 overstates the citation. The tool's SRC3.evap ('physics: heat ÷ latent heat; cycles … FEMP/EPA') is accurate.
evidence: energy.gov/node/849241 (fetched): the page "does not provide a latent heat value (h_fg), an evaporation figure in litres per kWh, or any reference to ISO 30134-9 or WUE"; sources/15a line 21.
suggested_fix: Cite h_fg to a steam-table or ASHRAE source (gap in 15a); keep FEMP only for the cycles and blowdown relation.

problem: Both ends of the make-up and blowdown ranges use the high evaporation figure (PUE 1.55). The low end (6 cycles) is therefore computed at PUE 1.55, not 1.4, which overstates it by about 11%. engine.js computes evap[0] but never uses it.
evidence: Recomputation: low make-up should be evap[0]×1.2 where evap[0]/evap[1] = 1.4/1.55 = 0.903.
suggested_fix: mk=[evap[0]*1.2, evap[1]*2], bd=[evap[0]/5, evap[1]/1] (or state that the range covers cycles only, at the high PUE).

tool_says: "O&M ≈ US$21/kW·yr, 30-yr life, 0.5–0.7 %/yr degradation (NREL, US)"; card: "degradation (0.5–0.7%/yr), O&M (about US$21/kW a year)" with sources list incl. nrel_bench2023
problem: These three figures come from NREL ATB 2024 Commercial PV (O&M about $21, 30 yr, 0.7%/yr) and NREL/PR-5200-56690 (0.5%/yr median). They do not come from the Q1 2023 cost benchmark (NREL/TP-7A40-87303), which is the only NREL source cited. That benchmark did not model commercial rooftop at all. The values themselves are correct.
evidence: atb.nrel.gov/electricity/2024/commercial_pv (fetched): "about $21/kWDC-yr for 2022", "30 years", "0.7%/yr in the baseline"; 87303 p.15: no commercial rooftop system modelled in Q1 2023.
suggested_fix: Add NREL ATB 2024 Commercial PV and NREL/PR-5200-56690 as sources for O&M, life and degradation.

tool_says: coef: "avoided carbon at the tool basis, NIR 2026 consumption intensity (2024): BC 18.1, Alberta 346.1"; sources: ["nrcan_pv2006","bc_ef2026","ab_ghgperf"]

The cited sources don't support the numbers stated. The worked shares (1.4–4.8 %, 0.28–0.96 %) were also computed with the 2006 yields 1009/1245, PUE 1.4–1.54 and no load factor. The tool uses 892–1007 / 944–1244, PUE 1.4–1.55 and load factor 0.6.
evidence: sources/15b §5 and §8; engine.js R.grid {van:18.1, edm:346.1}; addons.js:95 use = mw*PUE*8760*R.lf.

tool_says: cost=[kwp[0]*1000*rate(kwp[0])[0], kwp[1]*1000*rate(kwp[1])[1]]; display "at $${rate(kwp[0]).join('–')}/W"
problem: When the kWp range crosses a size band (100 or 250 kW), the high cost uses a different band from the $/W shown. Example: 90–112 kWp shows '$2–3.2/W', but the high cost uses 2.40. The figure shown doesn't match the arithmetic.
evidence: Recomputation: kwp=[90,112] → rate(90)=[2.0,3.2], rate(112)=[1.9,2.4]; cost high = 112,000×2.4, label says 2–3.2.
suggested_fix: Show both bands when they differ, e.g. '$2.00/W (low) to $2.40/W (high), by size band'.

tool_says: "generator housings give about 10–15 dB over a weather housing (Cummins, maker)"
problem: The register marks the 10–15 dB as 'Claude inference' (cumminsF1493), but the tool presents it as Cummins' own statement. F-1493 numbers give 90→80/76 = 10–14 dB. S-1443 (the corrected ranges) gives weather 89–91 vs L1 78–87 and L2 73–76, i.e. about 2–18 dB, so '10–15' is not robust across the two Cummins documents.
evidence: formula_register.json new_sources.cumminsF1493: "90 dB(A) weather housing, 80 Level I, 76 Level II acoustic (≈10–15 dB, Claude inference)"; noise_level coef: "QuietSite L2 73–76, L1 78–87, weather-protective 89–91 dBA @7 m".
suggested_fix: 'derived from Cummins F-1493 levels: about 10–14 dB for a 1,000 kW set (our arithmetic, maker data)'.

tool_says: "Kelvion dry cooler selection printout, EN 13487, Lw 94 dBA / 61 dBA @10 m"
problem: The verification_report correction ('do not cite 94 as a unit value') is applied in the noise_level coef and source role ('unit total unresolved'). The source string itself still states 'Lw 94 dBA' without the per-fan caveat. No tool JS displays kelvionLF, so the risk is only if the source list is shown. The other corrections checked were applied: Cummins S-1443 73–76 / 78–87 / 89–91 in the coef, Stulz 30–150 kW, and BC 22.8 consumption vs AB 335 generation in gridBC/gridAB. The tool now uses NIR 18.1/346.1 consumption for both cities.
evidence: verification_report.md item 5; formula_register.json noise_level coef and source_roles.
suggested_fix: Append '(printed under a per-fan heading; unit total unresolved)' to the kelvionLF source string.

tool_says: "3 → 6 cycles cuts make-up by 20% and blowdown by 50%"
problem: FEMP does say this (confirmed), but it contradicts the blowdown relation 15a derives and the register uses (B = E ÷ (C−1)). That relation gives E/2 → E/5, a 60% cut; the make-up cut of 20% does match. The 50% figure is not used in the tool, but should not be quoted alongside the formula without comment.
evidence: energy.gov/node/849241 (fetched): "Increasing cycles from three to six reduces cooling tower make-up water by 20% and cooling tower blowdown by 50%." Recomputation: 1/(3−1)=0.50, 1/(6−1)=0.20 → −60%.
suggested_fix: Quote FEMP's 50% as stated, and note that the register formula gives 60%.

tool_says: vancouver: 'approval'; edmonton: 'allowed' — edmonton text: "the 1.5 m height allowance is written for residential zones only, so industrial zones are not addressed — City to confirm"
problem: Edmonton gets 'allowed' even though its own text says the industrial-zone projection rule is unresolved ('City to confirm'). Vancouver gets 'approval' for a discretionary height relaxation. The asymmetry may be justified (no DP for a compliant collector, s. 7.120), but 'allowed' reads firmer than the evidence.
evidence: opps.json sources.edmZB510: "Non-residential zones: no projection limit stated — City to confirm".

Both values check out (BC Hydro tariff RS 1600–1611 'Energy Charge: 6.79 ¢ per kWh'; register aesoAMS2025 43.68). Whether an Edmonton data centre's energy charge equals pool price depends on its retail contract, which is not stated.
evidence: data/raw/bchydro/tariff.txt line 4773; formula_register.json aesoAMS2025.
suggested_fix: unverified — needs J.B. (label the Edmonton basis 'pool price; retail contract adds margin').

tool_says: svc=fac[1]>13?'above 13 MVA: ...':fac[1]>6.5?'above 6.5 MVA: ...' ; Edmonton: fac[1]*1000>2500?'above 2,500 kVA: ...'
problem: fac is average facility power in MW (IT × PUE), but it is compared directly with thresholds in MVA and kVA. That ignores power factor, and it uses a yearly-average PUE where peak demand is higher (the tool says so itself one line later). Both effects understate the connected load, so the feeder thresholds are crossed later than they should be. The thresholds themselves are correct.
evidence: BC Hydro Primary Guide R4 s. 2 (fetched): "exceeding 6.5 MVA in a 7.2/12.5 kV area or exceeding 13.0 MVA in a 14.4/25 kV area"; EPCOR CCG Table 3.1 (fetched): "demand load will exceed 2,500kVA to one building". Tool text: "PUE is a yearly average, so peak demand is higher".
suggested_fix: unverified — needs J.B. (needs a power-factor and peak assumption). At minimum, say the comparison uses MW as an approximation of MVA.

where: tool/engine.js mathNeeds / fitsView fuel (fac × 12 h × 0.263) vs opps.json/formula_register.json 'fuel_on_site' formula; tool/decide.js:125
tool_says: Tool: "Standby fuel: {fac} MW × 1,000 (kW) × 12 h × 0.263 L per kWh"; decide.js: "Diesel kept on site to run the generators for 12 hours at full load."; register formula: "generator capacity × runtime hours × fuel per kWh"
problem: The register sizes fuel on generator capacity, but the tool uses average facility power (IT × yearly PUE). Generator capacity is larger than that (report 16: CAL-1 has 12 MW of gensets for 9 MW total power, and Uptime requires gensets to carry the full design load). So "at full load" overstates what the arithmetic shows, and the fuel figure is low.
evidence: sources/16 §3: "Generator MW per 'total power' MW: CAL-1 12 ÷ 9 = 1.33"; S7: gensets "must be large enough to carry the entire data center load".
suggested_fix: unverified — needs J.B. Either size on generator capacity, as the register says, or reword the text to "at the average facility load".

tool_says: "One spare (N+1) ... (like Tier II–III)"; "Double (2N) — Two independent systems (like Tier IV)"
problem: Report 16 says the public Uptime text defines Tier III as N+1 and Tier IV as fault tolerant (N+1+), and that "2N is not defined in the public Uptime text". The register's uptimeTiers entry says the N+1/2N-to-Tier mapping "is Claude's reading", but the user-facing card shows it without that caveat.

suggested_fix: "... conditional in I-2, I-1C, I-3 sub-area A and FC-2; not listed for other standard districts in the City's reference table; ODP areas not reviewed; CD-1 site-specific."

where: tool/engine.js:181–183 and 216 (fitsView 'Standby fuel' row); register condition b_fuel note (formula_register.json ~11732)
tool_says: a ${pos==='ground'?'first-storey':'basement or upper-storey'} room may hold ${fmt(fuelLim)} L${fuel[1]>fuelLim?' — more than one room or an outdoor tank':''}  [with R.fuelLimit:{low:20000,first:200000}; pos is '' for new builds and whole-building cases]
problem: (a) For new builds and whole-building retrofits, pos is empty, so the tool always applies the 20,000 L basement or upper-storey limit. It never considers a first-storey room (200,000 L), which is where generators usually go on a new build. (b) The tool also leaves out the NFC row that allows 45,000 L in a basement or upper-storey room when individual tanks exceed 20,000 L. Result: from about 5 MW IT (12 h × 0.263 L/kWh × 1.4–1.55 PUE ≈ 22,000–24,500 L) the tool says 'more than one room or an outdoor tank', which overstates the code limit. The b_fuel note has the same gap: 'more pushes fuel to the first storey or outdoor tanks'.

suggested_fix: Show 20,000 L (tanks ≤ 20,000 L) or 45,000 L (larger tanks) for a basement or upper storey. For new builds, show the first-storey limit of 200,000 L, or state which storey is assumed. The values are confirmed from NFC 2020 Table 4.3.13.4.-B.

tool_says: the data centre's heat still needs lifting to the network's 65 °C (By-law 9552)

The 65 °C minimum comes from the NEU Connectivity Guidelines (register source neuConnect), so it is attributed to the wrong document. cards.js:118 also gives the SEFC NEU as '67 °C supply, 50 °C return', which differs from 65 °C.

suggested_fix: Cite the NEU Connectivity Guidelines (May 2026) for 65 °C, not By-law 9552.

where: tool/engine.js:181, :294 (fuel calc); decide.js:125; formula_register fuel_on_site formula
tool_says: decide.js: 'Diesel kept on site to run the generators for 12 hours at full load.' engine.js: fuel = MW × PUE(1.4–1.55) × 1000 × 12 × 0.263
problem: The register formula is 'generator capacity × runtime hours × fuel per kWh'. The tool instead uses IT MW × the yearly-average PUE, which the same card calls 'Average power drawn ... PUE is a yearly average, so peak demand is higher'. The result is average facility draw, not generator capacity or full load. The label 'at full load' does not match the input, and generator redundancy (N+1) is not counted. The figure is low compared with the register's own formula.
evidence: engine.js:213 text: 'servers × PUE 1.4–1.55; PUE is a yearly average, so peak demand is higher'. Register fuel_on_site formula: 'generator capacity × runtime hours × fuel per kWh'. Arithmetic checked: 8.40 × 1000 × 12 × 0.263 = 26,510 L; 9.30 → 29,351 L (correct as computed).
suggested_fix: Make the formula and the label agree: either size on generator capacity as the register says, or relabel as 'at average facility load'. The correct sizing basis is unverified — needs J.B.

tool_says: In the designated floodplain: flood construction level 4.6 m. Switchgear and electrical rooms may not sit below it unless flood-protected — this mostly rules against a basement data centre.
problem: (a) The by-law names furnaces, electrical switchgear, electrical panels and fire protection systems, and requires them to be protected AND 'accessible for servicing during a flood'. 'Electrical rooms' is broader than the text, and the servicing condition is dropped. (b) 'Mostly rules against a basement data centre' goes further than note 22, which says to treat this as 'a constraint flag, not a ban on the basement option'. (c) The GVRD datum is missing, although note 22 says the tool should store '4.6 m (GVRD datum)'.
evidence: F014 (https://guidelines.vancouver.ca/F014.pdf, fetched 17 Oct): 'No person shall install furnaces, electrical switchgear, electrical panels, fire protection systems' ... 'accessible for servicing during a flood'; s.4.0 '4.6 m from GVRD datum'. sources/22 §1.4: 'Treat this as a constraint flag, not a ban on the basement option.'
suggested_fix: 'flood construction level 4.6 m (GVRD datum). Switchgear, electrical panels, furnaces and fire protection may not sit below it unless flood-protected and serviceable during a flood (VBBL 2.2.9.3(2)) — a constraint on a basement data centre.'

tool_says: report: '**F014 ss. 3.1.1 and 3.3** (industrial): "Main electrical switchgear shall be no lower than the FCL."' register: 'main switchgear in industrial buildings at or above FCL (F014 s. 3.3)'

A data centre zoned industrial may therefore face a lower floor requirement than 4.6 m.

The s.3.3 summary from the fetch tool: industrial uses except main electrical switchgear no lower than FCL minus freeboard; switchgear no lower than FCL (paraphrased by the fetch tool, not a verbatim quote).
suggested_fix: Cite s.3.3 only and add 'industrial floors may sit at FCL minus freeboard; main switchgear at FCL'. Verify the verbatim wording of s.3.3 from the PDF — needs J.B.

where: tool/engine.js:486 (Energy tab, EV charging); same formula at tool/opps.js:53–54; register ev_stalls.formula
tool_says: ${fmt(500/19.2)}–${fmt(500/7.4)} Level 2 stalls (7.4–19.2 kW at a 0.5 diversity), about ${fmt(500/19.2*22)}–${fmt(500/7.4*22)} m² of parking
problem: The 0.5 factor is applied the wrong way round. The register formula is 'P_reserved × SF ÷ P_charger', so 1 MW gives 26–68 stalls. A simultaneity factor of 0.5 means only half the chargers draw at once, so the same 1 MW supports n = P ÷ (P_charger × SF). That is four times more stalls (104–270) and four times more parking. The tool's text and the register share the error.
evidence: sources/06_opportunity_coefficients.md:16: Silber et al. 2024, 'Simultaneity factor 0.5 "in most cases"'. Simultaneity factor = coincident peak ÷ sum of connected loads. Recomputed: 1000/(19.2×0.5)=104.2; 1000/(7.4×0.5)=270.3. Tool: 500/19.2=26.0; 500/7.4=67.6.
suggested_fix: unverified — needs J.B. (if SF is the Silber simultaneity factor, stalls = 1,000 kW ÷ (7.4–19.2 kW × 0.5) ≈ 104–270, and parking scales to match)

where: tool/engine.js:475 and 484 (Energy tab, 'The batteries it already has'), at the default mw=1

evidence: Node check: f1(0.00833)='0.0' and f1(0.04167)='0.0', so rng returns '0.0 MWh'. The math box uses n1 (toFixed(2)) and gives '0.01–0.04 MWh'.

tool_says: engine.js: wbe=[MWh[0]*1000*1.25/1000,MWh[1]*1000*16.8/1000] for both cities; addons.js: Edmonton 'about '+fmt(MWh[1]*1.6)+' m³' (Alberta 2021: 85% coal and gas at ~1.25 L/kWh, 3% hydro at ~16.8)

tool_says: 24.5 m² of unit per MW of heat (register: component_space, manufacturer claims), so about 1.2 MW a unit
problem: 24.5 m²/MW comes from one unit rated at warm, liquid-cooling water (48→42.7 °C fluid). The research note says air-cooled water temperatures need much more area. tool_says: engine: 'dry coolers ${p.dry[0]}) = … m² per MW; × ${mw} = …' (IT MW); plant.js: '24.5 m² of unit per MW of heat' with Q = mw × 1.55
problem: The same component_space constant (24.5 m² dry cooler per MW) is applied per MW of IT load in engine.js but per MW of heat (IT × PUE 1.55) in plant.js. Dry-cooler area therefore differs by 1.55× between the What-fits and Needs pages and the set-up model.
evidence: At 12 MW, engine dry-cooler share = 24.5 × 12 = 294 m². plant.js = 16 units (ceil(18.6/1.1755)) × 28.8 = 461 m² before spares, 490 m² with N+1. The source basis is per MW of heat rejected (737.6 kW unit, sources/16 l.203).
suggested_fix: Use one basis. The source supports per MW of heat (× PUE) in engine.js. Confirm with J.B.

tool_says: plant.js: 'heat to reject ≈ ${mwT} × PUE 1.55 = ${Q} MW at peak.'; engine.js: 'Average power at the meter: ${mw} MW × PUE …'
problem: The same product (IT MW × PUE) is called 'at peak' in plant.js and 'Average power' in engine.js:163. engine.js:470 multiplies it by load factor 0.6 to get annual MWh, which treats it as peak. Also, the register defines PUE as an annual energy ratio, not a peak-power ratio.
evidence: engine.js:470 'MWh=[fac[0]*8760*R.lf, …]'. Register pue formula: 'E_facility ÷ E_IT'.
suggested_fix: Unverified, needs J.B. (probably label engine.js:163 as peak, and note that PUE is an annual ratio).

tool_says: Sized for 12 MW of servers …: heat to reject ≈ 12 × PUE 1.55 = 19.1 MW at peak.
problem: For sizes ≥10 MW the factor is rounded to whole MW, but Q uses the unrounded size, so the printed arithmetic is wrong. 12 × 1.55 = 18.6, not 19.1. This only happens with the provisional (continuous) size; MW steps ≥10 are whole numbers.
suggested_fix: Print the multiplier with one decimal (12.3), or compute Q from the rounded value.

tool_says: BD.geo.rectW(F,p.u-p.L/2-1,p.u+p.L/2+1,p.v-p.W/2-1,p.v+p.W/2+1)
problem: In the second, rotated pass the units from the first pass are blocked only by a 1 m pad, so new and old units can sit closer than the manufacturer gap. where: tool/cards.js:37 (ECON.fixed) and the display at :195, :197, :245; used in every connection card's cost, break-even and payback
tool_says: fixed:112611,           // City of Vancouver NEU connection levy 2025, fixed part per energy transfer station (+ $133/kW of peak, not included ...)

where: tool/cards.js:187 (connection card, 'This building takes'); affects every non-housing receiver with floor area (all 309 Edmonton receivers with fa; 155 in Vancouver)
tool_says: `about ${fmt(x.demand)} MWh/yr (${p.u} homes × ${R.homeMWh[city]} MWh, provincial average for space and hot water) — ...`
problem: When x.demand is set, the line always uses the housing wording. For schools, hospitals, care homes, rec centres, pools and arenas, demand comes from floor area × CEUD, and p.u is undefined. The card therefore prints 'undefined homes × 29.19 MWh' and names the wrong method. Every Edmonton receiver is non-housing, so every Edmonton connection card with a floor area shows this.

tool_says: const share=x.demand?[x.demand/r.avail[1],Math.min(1,x.demand/r.avail[0])]:null; ... ${Math.round(share[0]*100)}–${Math.round(share[1]*100)}% of what is offered
problem: Only the high end is capped at 100%. When the building's demand is larger than the most heat offered, the range prints low above high, for example '474–100%'. This happens with real receivers at the default 1 MW: avail is 3,244–5,913 MWh, and the largest Vancouver housing record (1,924 homes × 14.58 = 28,052 MWh) gives 474–100%. A school above about 16,300 m² in Edmonton also exceeds it.
suggested_fix: Cap both ends (Math.min(1,…)) and say 'more than all of it' when demand exceeds avail[1]

where: tool/opps.js:53 (EV charging hub, physics gate); same formula at tool/engine.js:486 and formula_register.json ev_stalls

problem: The factor 0.5 is applied the wrong way round. The register's source term is a 'simultaneity 0.5' (Silber 2024). A simultaneity factor is the share of chargers drawing power at the same moment, so peak = n × P_charger × 0.5. That gives n = P ÷ (0.5 × P_charger). The tool uses n = P × 0.5 ÷ P_charger, which is 4 times too few stalls. The register formula 'P_reserved × SF ÷ P_charger' has the same inversion.
evidence: formula_register.json ev_stalls source_roles: silber2024 'simultaneity 0.5'; sources/06_opportunity_coefficients.md l.16 'Simultaneity factor | 0.5 "in most cases"' (only the abstract was read). Recomputed: 1000/(0.5×19.2)=104; 1000/(0.5×7.4)=270 stalls, against the tool's 26–68.
suggested_fix: If Silber's definition is coincident peak ÷ connected load: stalls = P ÷ (SF × P_charger) = about 104–270 for 1 MW. Unverified — needs J.B. to confirm the definition in the Silber full text.

tool_says: about 3,609 m³ of rain a year on the roof  (Edmonton example)
problem: For a new building, roofArea() uses the parcel ring × 0.86 × 0.86 (10,676 m²), not the modelled footprint that is drawn (M.footArea 13,075 m²). In the Edmonton example the roof used is 18% smaller than the building shown. At 1425 Clark Dr the gap is 1% (4,315 against 4,356 m²).
evidence: out_1.json: roof 10676.2, footArea 13075.2. Recomputed: 10,676 × 0.4225 × 0.8 = 3,609 m³; with the footprint, 13,075 × 0.4225 × 0.8 = 4,419 m³.
suggested_fix: Use M.footArea (or the server footprint) when the model exists. Unverified — needs J.B.

tool_says: about ${fmt(rain)} m³ of rain a year on the roof  [mm = 1159.5 van / 422.5 edm]
problem: Both figures are total precipitation, snow included, but the text calls them 'rain'. For Edmonton City, rainfall is 329.3 mm of the 422.5 mm, so 'rain' is overstated by about 28%. Register coef: 'Dec–Feb 43 mm, mostly snow'.
evidence: data/normals_1991_2020_extract.json: EDMONTON (CITY) Precipitation 422.5, Rainfall 329.3; VANCOUVER INTL Precipitation 1159.5, Rainfall 1119.2.
suggested_fix: Say 'rain and snow (precipitation)', or use rainfall: 1,119.2 mm Vancouver, 329.3 mm Edmonton City.

tool_says: Edmonton has 6.1–6.5 days a year at or below −20 °C (ECCC Normals 1991–2020)  /  Vancouver: no days at −20 °C
problem: 6.1–6.5 counts days when the daily maximum stays at or below −20 °C. 'At or below −20 °C' reads as days that reach −20 °C, which are many more. The register says 'daily max ≤ −20 °C'.
evidence: normals extract: 'Days with Maximum Temperature <= -20 °C' Edmonton City 6.1, Edmonton Airport 6.5, Vancouver Intl 0.0. Register refuge_people: '6.1–6.5 days/yr with daily max ≤ −20 °C'.
suggested_fix: '6.1–6.5 days a year that stay at or below −20 °C all day (daily maximum)'; Vancouver: 'no such days'.

suggested_fix: 'Smaller, and fewer at larger sizes'.

where: tool/explain.js:149 (people card, 'How far it carries here')
tool_says: The night limit of 55 dBA is reached at 36–112 m
problem: For Vancouver, lim is the limit at a quiet-zone neighbour for this source zone (activity → quiet 55); other receivers have 65. For Edmonton, 50 is the residential limit (60 non-residential). The panel says which receiver the limit applies to; the card does not. The Vancouver intermediate → quiet value of 50 used in the code is not in the register (it lists only quiet→quiet 55/45, activity→quiet 60/55, other 70/65), so it is unverified.
evidence: formula_register.json noise_limit formula: 'Vancouver by zone pair, continuous: quiet→quiet 55/45, activity→quiet 60/55, other 70/65'; Edmonton 's.20 residential night 50 … s.22 non-residential night 60'. engine.js:575 'at a quiet-zone neighbour'.
suggested_fix: 'The night limit at a home (quiet zone) of 55 dBA …'. Intermediate → quiet 50: unverified, needs J.B.

tool_says: they need the most space: 1 units for this size.
problem: No singular form: the text renders '1 units', and the chart notes render '1 units' / '1 cells'. With spares '2n' the step text reads 'with double spare'; 2N means the units are doubled, not that there is a 'double spare'.
evidence: Rendered example 0 and 1 at 0.3 MW: 'Dry coolers: 29 m² of units — 1 units'; at 10 MW 2N: 'Units for 10 MW, with double spare.'
suggested_fix: Pluralise on n; say 'with every unit doubled (2N)'.

tool_says: marks:[[Math.min(600,dist[0]),'low-noise'],[Math.min(600,dist[1]),'standard',14]]
problem: Once a distance passes 600 m, its marker is pinned at the 600 m axis edge and still labelled as the distance where the limit is reached. The text gives the true value, but the chart doesn't show the clamp.
evidence: Recomputation, 40 MW Edmonton: n = round(62) = 62, Lw hi = 101 + 17.9 = 118.9, distance = 10^((118.9 − 8 − 50)/20) ≈ 1,112 m, but the marker sits at 600 m.

where: tool/explain.js:121 (heat card, 'What this size could offer')
tool_says: About 3.2–5.9 GWh a year, the space and water heating of 222–406 homes
problem: ctx() always calls calc with recover:true, so the card shows the liquid-cooled, heat-pumped figure even when the user hasn't chosen recovery. The panel says 'none — air-cooled heat at 25–35 °C goes to the air' in that case. The 'could' framing partly covers it. The arithmetic checks: 5,256 MWh × 0.48 × 4.5/3.5 = 3,244 MWh, ÷ 14.58 = 222; × 0.75 × 1.5 = 5,913 MWh, ÷ 14.58 = 406.

suggested_fix: Unverified intent — J.B. to decide whether to add 'if liquid-cooled and recovered'.

where: tool/extras.js:214 (site report, 'In numbers'); same pattern in engine.js:163, engine.js:213, addons.js:140, explain.js:128
tool_says: ['Average power at the meter',rng(fac[0],fac[1],'MW')]  with  fac=[mw*R.pue[0],mw*R.pue[1]]
problem: The label says 'average', but the value is peak IT MW × PUE with no load factor. Everywhere else the tool takes average IT load as mw × 0.6 (it=mw*8760*R.lf). So the 'average power' shown is 1/0.6 = 1.67× the average the tool itself uses for yearly MWh. At 1 MW the report prints 1.4–1.55 MW 'average', but its own yearly energy works out to 0.84–0.93 MW average.
evidence: Recomputed: 1 MW × 1.4 × 8760 × 0.6 = 7,358 MWh/yr, ÷ 8760 = 0.84 MW average (1.55 → 0.93 MW). Register load_factor: 'average ÷ peak ... ≈ 0.6 facility level (Fan et al. 2007); 8,760 h/yr'.
suggested_fix: Either relabel it as peak (e.g. 'Power at the meter at full IT load') or show mw × PUE × 0.6 = 0.84–0.93 MW per MW as the average. Which one is J.B.'s call. Fix the shared label in engine.js, addons.js and explain.js too.

where: tool/extras.js:118-122 (sensView MWof; 'Largest data centre that fits (this site)'); Edmonton worked example (12603 123 Street NW)
tool_says: const MWof=(s,m,len)=>(len&&f.hallL?Math.min(up,G*s):up*s)/m;  → rendered 'Hall area per MW 290–630 m² per MW 28–60 MW' and 'Hall share of floor 0.48–0.72 30–45 MW'
problem: What matters most does not apply the 40 MW cap that siteFacts uses (toMW=h=>[Math.min(40,…)]). On the Edmonton worked example, What fits shows 22–40 MW, while this page shows bars up to 60 MW and a middle case of about 38 MW. The two pages contradict each other on the same site.
evidence: Ran the page (playwright, example 1): rows read '28–60 MW' and '30–45 MW'. siteFacts for the same parcel: mw [22.12, 40], hallGross 29,032 m². Recomputed: 29,032 × 0.6 ÷ 290 = 60.1 MW; 29,032 × 0.72 ÷ 460 = 45.4 MW; engine.js:118 caps at 40.

where: tool/extras.js:187 (two cities, 'Busiest to quietest heating month'); also cards.js:211, engine.js:324
tool_says: ['Busiest to quietest heating month','about 3.9 : 1','about 3.3 : 1','total heat demand (CWEC)','peer']
problem: 3.9 and 3.3 come from a profile built on the national 61% space-heat share. The register says that share was replaced by provincial CEUD 2023 shares. With provincial shares the ratios change a lot, and the order between the cities can flip. The rounding is also off: the unrounded Vancouver value at 61% is 3.97, not 3.9. The badge 'research or government lab' fits poorly too: this is the tool's own calculation from CWEC with an assumed share.
evidence: data/cwec_derived.json: 'monthly_heat_share_space61' ... 'peak_month_over_min_month': 3.9 / 3.3. formula_register.json demand_profile: 'provincial space-heat share from CEUD 2023: BC 0.46, AB 0.63 (replaces national 0.61 in the profile)'. Recomputed from monthly_HDD16_share as peak ÷ min of s·HDD + (1−s)/12. Vancouver: 3.97 at s=0.61, 2.66 at s=0.46, 4.22 at s=0.63 (space ÷ space+water). Edmonton: 3.36 at 0.61, 3.54 at 0.631, 4.62 at 0.732.
suggested_fix: unverified — needs J.B. (first pick the share basis: share of all household energy, or space ÷ space+water heat to match homeMWh; then recompute both cities)

tool_says: 'downtown feeders frozen to 2032' / 'downtown Vancouver feeder freeze to 2032'
problem: This overstates the source. The CPCN says all 12 kV feeder positions will be in use by fiscal 2027, and that in the meantime BC Hydro will still connect customers with temporary measures. 2032 is when the proposed substation is expected in service, and the CPCN decision is still pending. 'Frozen' suggests no connections at all, ending on a fixed date.
evidence: data/BCH_West_End_Substation_CPCN_2025-11-10.pdf s.2.2.2: 'by fiscal 2027, all the 12 kV feeder positions in the Study Area will be in use'; 'To connect new customers in the interim period, BC Hydro will implement temporary measures'. Register grid_headroom: 'expected in service July 2032 ... decision pending'.
suggested_fix: e.g. 'downtown 12 kV feeder positions all in use by fiscal 2027; new customers only by temporary measures until a new substation (proposed, July 2032)'

where: tool/extras.js:191 (two cities, 'Night noise limit next to homes', Vancouver)

problem: The register's By-law 6555 reading puts R3-1–3, R4-1, R5-1–4 and RR-3A–C (residential zones) in the intermediate class. From an activity zone, the night limit to intermediate is 65 dBA, so homes in those zones can have a 65 dBA night limit. The 45–55 range covers only homes in quiet zones.

where: tool/extras.js:213-215 (site report rows 'Size tested' and 'Heat offered')
tool_says: ['Size tested',`${mw} MW of servers · ${f.density==='high'?'high-density, liquid-cooled halls':'typical air-cooled halls'}`] … ['Heat offered (liquid-cooled, heat pump)', …]
problem: With the default density, the report says the tested size is 'typical air-cooled halls'. Two rows later it gives heat offered on a liquid-cooled, heat-pump basis (calc with recover:true). A reader can take that heat to belong to the air-cooled building just described.
evidence: extras.js:208: r=e.calc({mw,recover:true,to:'near'},…); the liquid-capture share 0.48–0.75 applies only to direct-to-chip (register liquid_capture: 'air-cooled: no primary figure').

tool_says: Real data centres sit in the lower half of the range ... Only 11 buildings worldwide publish both IT load and floor area.
problem: 'Only 11 buildings worldwide' overclaims. 11 is the count of benchmark-tier entries in the tool's own catalogue (public or filed record). The same catalogue has 15 more references with the same pair from operator claims, and no global search can show that no others exist. 'Sit in the lower half' is also too strong: the benchmark p25 of 593 m²/MW lands in the upper half of the MW range.

suggested_fix: e.g. 'In the tool's catalogue, 11 buildings have IT load and floor area on public or filed record; most of them fall in the lower half of the range.'

where: tool/extras.js:176 (citiesView mw default) vs extras.js:115 (sensView) and extras.js:207 (siteReport)

tool_says: 'BC Hydro large general service 6.79 ¢/kWh + $13.83/kW a month' | 'Alberta pool averaged $43.68/MWh in 2025, plus wires charges'
problem: The two cities are given in different units, and the figures are different kinds of price: a BC retail energy rate plus a demand charge, against an Alberta wholesale pool average with no wires charges. Read side by side, 6.79 next to 43.68 is easy to misread.
evidence: 6.79 ¢/kWh = $67.90/MWh. Register electricity_price: 'BC LGS ... $13.83/kW, 6.79 ¢/kWh' and 'Alberta: pool $43.68/MWh (2025)'. Values match the register; only the presentation is in question.
suggested_fix: e.g. show both in $/MWh ('$67.90/MWh energy + $13.83/kW a month' vs '$43.68/MWh pool average + wires') and keep 'not like for like'

tool_says: data centres ≥75 MW may tether to their own new generation or storage
problem: The register's reading of Alta Reg 117/2026 s.5 defines 'tethered' as tied to a generating unit or storage facility of equal or greater capability. 'Own' and 'new' are not in that summary; 'new' comes from the government summary (self_gen_rules). I could not check the regulation text: the local PDF's text layer would not extract.
evidence: formula_register.json grid_headroom: "s.5 'tethered' = large data centre whose access request is tied to a generating unit or storage facility of equal or greater capability". pdftotext on data/Alta_Reg_117_2026_Data_Centre_Regulation.pdf gives garbled glyphs.
suggested_fix: unverified — needs J.B. (e.g. 'may tether to generation or storage of equal or greater capability (s. 5)')

tool_says: liquid to air: heat offered drops to none
problem: This states more than the register supports. The register gives no primary capture figure for air cooling ('air-cooled: no primary figure'). That is a gap in evidence, not evidence that heat offered becomes zero; air-cooled halls can supply heat through heat pumps on the air or chilled-water side.
evidence: formula_register.json liquid_capture: 'air-cooled: no primary figure'; 'A water-cooled chiller plant rejects all heat to the condenser loop'.
suggested_fix: e.g. 'liquid to air: heat offered falls to an unsourced share (none is modelled)'

where: tool/extras.js:116-118, 135-137 (what matters most, middle case and 'Not varied' lines)

The sourced floor-to-floor range of 5.5–6.0 m is neither varied nor listed as 'not varied'. tool_says: Middle case: floor-space ratio × lot, hall share 0.6, 460 m² of hall per MW; yards not applied.
problem: The legend leaves out two steps the code applies. Floor area is capped at lot × storeys, with storeys counted at a 5.75 m floor height (a value not stated anywhere). The ground floor is removed in I-2, I-3 and FC-2 (the strict reading). Both can lower a lot's bin.
evidence: extras.js:261-262: n=1+Math.max(0,Math.floor((env.h-6)/5.75)); G=Math.min(lot*fsr,lot*n); up=env.ground?G-G/n:G; p._mw=Math.min(40,up*0.6/460). 0.6 = mid of hallShare [0.48,0.72] and 460 = mid of m2PerMW [290,630] check out.

where: tool/site.js:121 (existing-building branch of model()); shown at site.js:204, 263 and in liveBox (site.js:193)
tool_says: { const big=...; m.foot=big?big.r:null; m.roofH=big?big.h:0; } // the roof the plant sits on is the largest part's own roof, at its own height m.feet=blds.map(b=>({r:b.r,h:b.h})); m.footArea=blds.reduce((t,b)=>t+b.a,0);
problem: The m.feet and m.footArea assignments sit inside the // comment, so they never run. footArea falls back to line 158 (area of the largest part only) and m.feet stays undefined. Result: for an existing building, step 2 ('The existing building: X m² in plan'), the setup summary ('Footprint X m² (existing)') and the live box show only the largest part. The site card and engine.siteFacts use the sum of all parts. plant.js:73 builds its no-go list for yard plant from m.feet, so the other existing buildings are never excluded. opps.js:28 'free' ground also subtracts only the largest part.
evidence: Ran 1425 Clark Dr (van-2_1-23060741) with answers.built='existing' (scratch/csi/t1.js). Three parts: 58, 558, 1,341 m². model().footArea = 1,341; m.feet = null; engine siteFacts f.foot = 1,956 and f.how = 'footprint 1,956 m² × about 1 storeys'. Summary text: 'Footprint 1,341 m² (existing)'. Site card: '3 footprints, 1,956 m² in plan'. On this lot the generator boxes did not overlap other buildings, so a plant overlap was not seen here. It is still possible because the no-go list is empty.
suggested_fix: Move 'm.feet=…; m.footArea=…;' out of the comment onto its own line (code change for J.B.; figure becomes 1,956 m² on 1425 Clark Dr).

where: tool/site.js:13-14 (ZV['I-2B'].fsr [3,4] and clause text); used as the high end of floor area via engine.js:80, 86
tool_says: 'I-2B':{fsr:[3,4], ... ['Floor area','up to 3.0 × the lot; the Director of Planning or Development Permit Board may allow 4.0','I-2 ss. 3.2.1.1–2 (sub-area B)']
problem: In sub-area B, s. 3.2.1.2 raises the TOTAL FSR to 4.00, but the s. 3.2.1.1(a) cap of 3.00 for transportation and storage uses (which includes Bulk Data Storage) still applies. The increase also depends on at least 1.00 FSR of s. 3.2.1.1(c) uses. So a data centre cannot use 4.0. The tool treats 4.0 as data-centre floor area. This inflates the high end of floor area, MW and loading count for sub-area B.
evidence: data/raw/codes/van_I-2_schedule.txt, p.13 s. 3.2.1.1(a): 'the maximum floor space ratio is 3.00 for: … (iv) transportation and storage uses'. p.14 s. 3.2.1.2: 'may increase the total maximum floor space ratio to 4.00' with condition '(a) the provision of a minimum floor space ratio of 1.00 combined for any uses listed in section 3.2.1.1(c)'. Run on 1425 Clark Dr with subB='1': Z.fsr = [3,4], f.how = 'lot 5,845 m² × floor-space ratio 3–4'.
suggested_fix: Data-centre FSR ceiling in sub-area B is 3.00 (s. 3.2.1.1(a)); the 4.00 total is reachable only with ≥1.00 FSR of other listed uses — describe it that way rather than 'may allow 4.0'.

where: tool/site.js:19 (ZV['FC-2'] h:22.9, fsr [1,5]); site.js:218 hmode label
tool_says: 'FC-2':{fsr:[1,5],h:22.9,hx:[51.8,51.8], ...}  and the option text `Outright: ${Z.hOutright} m` — 'what the zone allows without the City's discretion'
