The clause table does say '10.7–22.9 m by sub-area', but the number used and labelled 'outright' is the maximum.
evidence: data/raw/van/fc2.txt: s. 3.1.2.1 'Maximum building height 22.9 m' (sub-areas A/B); s. 3.2.2.1 and s. 3.3.2.1 'Maximum building height 10.7 m'. sources/17 update table: C1/C2/D '10.7 m'.
suggested_fix: unverified — needs J.B. (either a sub-area choice like I-2, or label 22.9 m as the highest sub-area value and show 10.7 m as the low end)

where: tool/index.html:563 (Vancouver lot-area fallback) vs site.js:110 / engine.js:70 (Edmonton lot = a[4] only)
tool_says: Vancouver: 'lot area: the tax report's figure, unless it is missing or under half the measured outline … then the outline that was picked, measured'. Edmonton: const lotArea=city==='van'?(...):(+a[4]||0);
problem: Parity gap. Vancouver falls back to the measured outline when the record is missing or implausibly small. Edmonton always uses the assessment record's lot area, even when a measured title-lot outline is loaded. So Edmonton lots can show a tiny lot area and floor area while the drawn footprint covers the whole outline.
evidence: scratch/csi/edmlot2.py over tool/tiles/edm: 289 lots ≥100 m² have a record under half the outline (47 of them in IH/IM/BE); 1,564 have a record over twice the outline. Browser check, 8811 56 Ave NW (IM, tile 0_-3, id 112829): record lot 14 m², outline 32,305 m². model().lotArea = 14, gross = [28, 28] m², mw ≈ 0.02–0.07, while footArea = 32,140 m².
suggested_fix: unverified — needs J.B. (apply the same 'record < ½ outline → measured' rule to Edmonton, or warn)

where: tool/index.html:528 and :537 (Edmonton lot pick) → select() at :559
tool_says: const A=cT.A; const id=lot.p.ids.slice().sort((u,v)=>((A[v]||[])[4]||0)-((A[u]||[])[4]||0))[0]; ... return select({city:'edm',tile:cT.key,id,...})
problem: A lot outline in an l_<tile>.json file can list assessment ids that are stored only in a NEIGHBOURING tile's A table. When none of a lot's ids are in its own tile, select() reads T.A[id] as undefined. The card then shows 'No civic address', zone blank ('Special area'), 'Lot area: — m²'. Lot area is 0 and siteFacts gross/MW come out NaN.
evidence: scratch/csi/edmlot2.py: 544 lots whose chosen id is missing from their own tile but present in another tile. Browser check, tile -1_-1 lot 110 (id 956386): sel.a = null, lotArea = 0, zone '', gross = [NaN, NaN] (serialised as null), side text 'No civic address … Special area zone … Lot area: — m²'.
suggested_fix: Look the id up across loaded tiles (or pass the record's own tile key) — code change for J.B.

where: tool/site.js:134-135, :97 (loading basis text); seen on 1425 Clark Dr
tool_says: 9 truck loading bays for 17,535 m² of floor.
problem: The loading count uses lot × the zone's maximum FSR (gfaGuess = lotArea*Z.fsr[1]), not the building's floor area. The same drawer's live box shows the floor area that fits as 13,068 m². At 13,068 m² the same rule gives 7 bays, not 9. The wording reads as the building's floor area. The count also ignores storeys, coverage or a chosen size.

tool_says: const n=gfa<100?0:1+(gfa>465?1:0)+Math.max(0,Math.ceil((gfa-2325)/2325));
problem: Two parts of the rule are not in the register or source 17. (1) The 100 m² zero threshold. (2) Rounding up ('any portion') for each further 2,325 m². The register says 'one per further 2,325 m²'; source 17 says 'plus 1 for each further 2,325 m²'. If the by-law means whole multiples, the count drops by one in most cases. Parking By-law s. 5 is not in data/ to check.
evidence: formula_register.json source vanParking5: 'one space for the first 465 m² plus one for the next 1,860 m² and one per further 2,325 m²'. sources/17 §3: 'plus 1 for each further 2,325 m²'. No 100 m² threshold appears in either.
suggested_fix: unverified — needs J.B. (check bylaws.vancouver.ca/parking/sec05.pdf row 5.2.5 wording)

where: tool/engine.js:16 (R.ftf.ground 6.0) used by site.js:118, 125 for I-2
tool_says: ftf:{ground:6.0, up:[5.5,6.0]},     // ground: zoning minimum (I-2/I-3) and Burlington
problem: The I-2 minimum first-floor height is 6.1 m (sub-area A s. 3.1.2.4, sub-area B s. 3.2.2.9), not 6.0 m. Only I-3 and FC-2 are 6.0 m. where: engine.js:213 (What fits step) and addons.js:140 (Electricity step headline); parcel 1425 Clark Dr (harness arg 0)
tool_says: Average power drawn: 8.4–9.3 MW at the meter (servers × PUE 1.4–1.55; PUE is a yearly average, so peak demand is higher)  /  8.4–9.3 MW average power at the meter · 44–49 GWh a year
problem: The two headline figures contradict each other. If 8.4–9.3 MW were the average, a year would be 73.6–81.5 GWh, not 44–49. The 44–49 GWh figure applies load factor 0.6 (register: load_factor = average ÷ peak) to 8.4–9.3 MW. So 8.4–9.3 MW is the design (peak) power, and the true average is 5.0–5.6 MW. The $4.4–4.9M a year also bills 8.4–9.3 MW as the monthly demand, which treats it as the peak. Standby fuel (8.40–9.30 MW × 12 h at the full-load fuel rate) and the cooling-unit count (9.30 MW → 10 units) also use it as a peak. Only the label 'average' and the clause 'peak demand is higher' disagree with how the figure is used everywhere else.
evidence: Recomputed: 6 MW × 1.4 = 8.40 MW; 8.40 × 8,760 = 73,584 MWh, but the tool shows 8.40 × 8,760 × 0.6 = 44,150 MWh (44 GWh). 9.30 × 8,760 × 0.6 = 48,881 MWh (49 GWh). Cost: 44,150 MWh × $67.90 + 8,400 kW × $13.83 × 12 = $2.998M + $1.394M = $4.39M; high end 48,881 × 67.90 + 9,300 × 13.83 × 12 = $4.86M, which matches the tool's $4.4–4.9M. formula_register.json load_factor: 'average ÷ peak … ≈ 0.6 facility level (Fan et al. 2007)'.
suggested_fix: unverified — needs J.B. Either relabel 8.4–9.3 MW as design or peak power at the meter (average 5.0–5.6 MW), or drop the 0.6 load factor from energy, cost, CO₂e and heat. The two choices give very different headline figures.

All lot outlines, footprints and distances come out about 0.8% (Vancouver) to 0.9% (Edmonton) small in area. The fixed cos(lat0) adds up to about ±0.3% across Edmonton. This does not change any meaning, but the tool's 'measured' areas are systematically low.

suggested_fix: Use ellipsoidal factors (m/° lat ≈ 111,216 at 49.25°, ≈ 111,297 at 53.54°) or a UTM projection
